source.author: cic
source.text: quo usque tandem abutere, Catilina, patientia nostra?
source.text_original: quo usque tandem abutere, Catilina, patientia nostra?
source.text_english: How long, Catiline, will you abuse our patience?

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quamquam effeminatis auribus et gentilium odiis se nostri detractatione commendent carpentes ecclesiasticam disciplinam et patientia nostra quasi quodam temeritatis fomite abutentes, tamen aliquando taceant et quiescant et audiant prophetam dicentem: prohibe linguam tuam a malo et labia tua ne loquantur dolum, desiderentque ea sapere, quae digna sunt uita solitaria, et ecclesiae principem ac magistrum non contristent deum.
reuse.text_original: quamquam effeminatis auribus et gentilium odiis se nostri detractatione commendent carpentes ecclesiasticam disciplinam et patientia nostra quasi quodam temeritatis fomite abutentes, tamen aliquando taceant et quiescant et audiant prophetam dicentem: prohibe linguam tuam a malo et labia tua ne loquantur dolum, desiderentque ea sapere, quae digna sunt uita solitaria, et ecclesiae principem ac magistrum non contristent deum.
reuse.text_english: Although by their carping, by their disparagement of the Church’s discipline, and by their abuse of our patience as though it were some kindling of recklessness, they win the favor of effeminate ears and of the hatred of the heathen against us, still let them be silent for once and be still and listen to the prophet who says: Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking deceit, and let them desire to think those things that are worthy of the solitary life, and not grieve God, the ruler and teacher of the Church.
